articles.title: From Vaudeville to the Subway: How a Brooklyn Station Became a Kaleidoscopic Stage
articles.summary: Christopher Myers's glass mosaics at Church Avenue station resurrect Flatbush's unsung theater history. Featuring comedian Moms Mobley and Afro-Caribbean carnival figures, the panels are seen by over 10,000 daily riders. It's public art at its most democratic.

articles.title: Harry Styles's Orchestral Surprise: A Career-Defining Cover Steals the Show
articles.summary: At his curated Meltdown Festival, Harry Styles delivered an intimate orchestral set far from his Wembley run. His cover of "Bridge Over Troubled Water" has been hailed as the single greatest moment of his solo career, showcasing stunning vocal control.

articles.title: Abdullah Ibrahim, the Quiet Giant of Jazz Piano, Leaves a Legacy of Meditative Beauty
articles.summary: South African jazz pianist Abdullah Ibrahim, hailed by Nelson Mandela as his country's Mozart, has died at 91. His composition "Mannenberg" became an anti-apartheid anthem, and his fearless use of silence influenced generations of musicians.
